clauses.reason: The command is: "Executive Order No. 8616 of December 19, 1940, placing Palmyra Island under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy and reserving it for naval purposes, is hereby revoked." A revocation is performed when it takes effect; the order has no delayed effective date, so it was performed on signing, August 27, 1952. The command was exhausted on that date, and the lasting consequence is recorded in savings. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory treats the order as a single whole clause without isolating the operative words. The operative command is the single sentence from 'By virtue of the authority' to 'is hereby revoked.'; the order has no other command.

research_rationale:
EO 10388 (17 FR 7877; signed August 27, 1952; F.R. Doc. 52-9589) revokes Executive Order No. 8616 of December 19, 1940, which placed Palmyra Island under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy and reserved it for naval purposes: "Executive Order No. 8616 ... is hereby revoked." The command is a one-time act that took effect when the President signed it; it contains no delayed-effect wording, and the held Federal Register page prints it as signed August 27, 1952. Under the 2026-10-28 evidence ruling, the command is exhausted by performance on that date and the surviving consequence, that Executive Order No. 8616 no longer governs, is separated from the exhausted command and recorded in savings. The held text of Executive Order No. 8616 is an earlier instrument that this order revokes; it is not a later event.

savings.reason: The consequence of the revocation, that Executive Order No. 8616 no longer reserves Palmyra Island for naval purposes or places it under the Secretary of the Navy, is a surviving result of the performed act and not a continuing command of this order. Acts taken under Executive Order No. 8616 before the revocation are not undone by the order's text.
